column1: Which regex library underlies SQL Server 2025's regular expression functions?
column2:
RE2.
RE2 defines which syntax the SQL functions accept. A pattern copied from another regex engine can use features that RE2 does not support.
Review source

column1: What database compatibility level does SQL Server 2025 REGEXP_LIKE require?
column2:
170 or higher.
Running SQL Server 2025 is not sufficient if this database still uses an older compatibility level. Check the database setting.
Review source

column1: How is REGEXP_LIKE used in a SQL Server WHERE clause?
column2:
As a predicate: WHERE REGEXP_LIKE(ColumnName, 'pattern').
Use the function directly as the WHERE condition. No comparison to an integer return value is needed.
Review source

column1: With the default regex flags, why put ^ and $ around a grouped validation expression?
column2:
To require a match across the entire input string.
Anchors rule out matching only part of the input. Group alternatives so both anchors apply to the entire allowed pattern.
Review source

column1: In SQL Server regex, what does . match when the s flag is absent?
column2:
One character other than a newline.
The dot is a wildcard for one character under those rules. Add the s flag if that wildcard must include a newline.
Review source

column1: Which characters does SQL Server regex \w match?
column2:
ASCII letters, digits, and underscore: [0-9A-Za-z_].
For example, it matches a letter or underscore in an identifier. Use a Unicode class when broader character coverage is needed.
Review source

column1: In SQL Server 2025, what controls whether a regex ignores letter case?
column2:
The regex flags, such as c or i.
Use i to ignore case and c for case-sensitive matching. Do not rely on a case-insensitive SQL collation for regex behavior.
Review source

column1: Why does (?=...) fail in a SQL Server 2025 regex matching pattern?
column2:
The RE2 engine does not support lookahead.
Lookahead tests what follows without consuming it. SQL Server's RE2-based matching syntax does not implement that construct.
Review source

column1: Why can you not use \1 inside a SQL Server matching pattern to repeat a previously captured value?
column2:
RE2 does not support backreferences inside matching patterns.
A pattern backreference asks the matcher to repeat a previously matched value. Replacement strings can still refer to capture groups.
Review source

column1: Which SQL Server 2025 function replaces text selected by a regex pattern?
column2:
REGEXP_REPLACE().
Use it when the text to replace depends on a pattern, such as a run of whitespace.
Review source

column1: How many matching occurrences does REGEXP_REPLACE replace by default?
column2:
All matching occurrences.
For example, a digit pattern can replace digits in several positions. Specify an occurrence when you need to target only one.
Review source

column1: What does REGEXP_REPLACE return when no pattern match exists?
column2:
The original input string.
With no match, there is nothing to replace. Unlike SUBSTR, REPLACE is not looking for a single extracted value to return.
Review source

column1: What does an empty replacement string do in REGEXP_REPLACE?
column2:
Removes the matched substrings.
The function keeps the surrounding text and substitutes nothing for each selected match. This deletes only the matched portion.
Review source

column1: Which SQL Server 2025 function extracts one matching substring?
column2:
REGEXP_SUBSTR().
Use it to pull out one digit run or a captured group. Use REGEXP_MATCHES if you need all matches as rows.
Review source

column1: What does REGEXP_SUBSTR return when no match exists?
column2:
NULL.
NULL signals that no substring matched. It is not an unchanged copy of the input.
Review source

column1: In REGEXP_SUBSTR, what does occurrence = 2 select when the pattern matches several times?
column2:
Which matching occurrence to return.
An occurrence of 2 selects the second match. The group argument then chooses which part of that match to return.
Review source

column1: How does the group argument of REGEXP_SUBSTR choose a part of the selected match?
column2:
Which capture group's text to return.
Group 0 selects the whole match. A numbered group selects the part captured by the corresponding parentheses.
Review source

column1: Which SQL Server 2025 function returns a match's starting position by default?
column2:
REGEXP_INSTR().
Use it when you need a character position rather than the matched text. Its default return option points to the start.
Review source

column1: What position does REGEXP_INSTR use for a match at the first character?
column2:
1.
Positions are one-based. A zero result therefore does not refer to the first character.
Review source

column1: What does REGEXP_INSTR return when no match exists?
column2:
0.
Zero is the no-match sentinel. A valid match can begin at position 1 or later.
Review source

column1: Which SQL Server 2025 function counts matches of a regex pattern?
column2:
REGEXP_COUNT().
The result counts matches, not characters covered by those matches. A run of digits can count as one match.
Review source

column1: How many digit runs does REGEXP_COUNT('A12 B345','\d+') find?
column2:
2.
The pattern has one match for 12 and one for 345. Adjacent digits are part of the same run.
Review source

column1: Which SQL Server 2025 function splits text into rows using a delimiter pattern?
column2:
REGEXP_SPLIT_TO_TABLE().
Use a regex delimiter when separators can vary. The table-valued function returns the text tokens as rows.
Review source

column1: If a nonempty string has no delimiter match, what does REGEXP_SPLIT_TO_TABLE return?
column2:
One row containing the original string.
With nothing to split on, the entire nonempty input is one token.
Review source

column1: What does a REGEXP_SPLIT_TO_TABLE ordinal tell you about the token before sorting the returned rows?
column2:
The token's 1-based position in the input.
The ordinal records where the token occurred before splitting. Add ORDER BY ordinal when output order matters.
Review source

column1: Which APPLY operator expands each product's Tags into rows with REGEXP_SPLIT_TO_TABLE?
column2:
CROSS APPLY.
Apply the splitter to each product's Tags value. CROSS APPLY drops a product if the function returns no token rows.
Review source

column1: Which SQL Server 2025 function returns all pattern matches as a rowset?
column2:
REGEXP_MATCHES().
This returns one row per match rather than a single substring. It also exposes information about captured groups.
Review source

column1: What does REGEXP_MATCHES return when no match exists?
column2:
No rows.
An empty rowset differs from a row whose match_value is NULL. Account for that when choosing CROSS APPLY or OUTER APPLY.
Review source

column1: Which REGEXP_MATCHES column contains the complete matched text?
column2:
match_value.
The column contains the whole match. Use the capture information when you need only a parenthesized part.
Review source

column1: Which REGEXP_MATCHES column describes the captured parts as JSON rather than containing the entire match?
column2:
substring_matches.
The JSON describes individual capture groups rather than the complete match text. Keep match_value for the full substring.
Review source
